key_insight: ActSpace-Bench tests whether vision-language models can actively seek the visual evidence needed to answer spatial questions, rather than reason only from images provided to them. It contains 994 questions across 234 exploration episodes in 72 real-scanned indoor scenes.
problem_solved: Conventional image and video evaluations do not directly test whether a model can decide where to look when the evidence needed for spatial reasoning is initially out of view.
method: Start the model from a single view in a real-scanned indoor scene.
Let it navigate real captured frames to seek evidence relevant to a spatial question.
Evaluate purposeful exploration and spatial question answering across diverse scenes and episodes.
impact: The benchmark offers a way to assess evidence-seeking behavior relevant to embodied assistants and navigation systems. The provided abstract is truncated, so specific performance findings are not available.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison: answering from supplied images versus actively seeking relevant views.
Indoor floor-plan diagram showing a starting viewpoint, exploration path, and evidence location.
Three metric cards: 994 questions, 234 episodes, and 72 indoor scenes.
Process diagram: spatial question → choose where to look → gather evidence → answer.
paper_title: Seeking in Space: Benchmarking Purposeful Active Exploration of Vision-Language Models for Spatial Reasoning
paper_authors: Xiwei Liu, Yulong Li, Xuhui Li, Xinlin Zhuang, Zhixiang Lu
